plants.name: Platycerium bifurcatum
plants.tip: The brown shield frond at the back is alive. Peeling it off strips the plant of its own root cover.
plants.colour: Grey-green forked fronds over a tan shield

plants.name: Platycerium hillii
plants.tip: Water the mount, not the crown. It clumps freely, so pups can be cut off once they have a shield of their own.
plants.colour: Broad dark green fronds, pale green shield

plants.name: Platycerium veitchii
plants.tip: The silver coat is living hair that shades the frond. Do not wipe it, and water at the base rather than overhead.
plants.colour: Silver-white furred fronds, held upright

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii
plants.tip: Wants steady humidity and a mount it can dry out on. Soak it, then let the moss go light before soaking again.
plants.colour: Narrow silver-grey fronds hanging in ribbons

plants.name: Platycerium alcicorne
plants.tip: Small enough to dry out fast on a bare mount. Check the moss twice a week rather than watering to a schedule.
plants.colour: Mid-green, lightly forked fronds, tan shield

plants.name: Platycerium superbum
plants.tip: One growing bud only, hidden behind the shield. Water sitting there rots it, so soak the mount and keep the crown dry.
plants.colour: Light green antlers above a large brown crown shield

plants.name: Platycerium grande
plants.tip: Single-budded like superbum, with no pups to fall back on. Err towards under-watering through winter.
plants.colour: Pale green forked fronds over a broad brown nest

plants.name: Platycerium wandae
plants.tip: It gets very heavy. Mount it on something that will still hold once the nest frond fills with debris and water.
plants.colour: Deep green fronds over a very large tan nest

plants.name: Platycerium coronarium
plants.tip: Needs warmth and hanging room for the long fertile fronds. Cold and wet through winter is what kills it.
plants.colour: Green fronds with long pendent spore lobes

plants.name: Platycerium ridleyi
plants.tip: Rot at the bud is the usual death. Keep humidity high, air moving, and the ridged shield itself dry.
plants.colour: Glossy green ridged shield, narrow upright fronds

plants.name: Platycerium holttumii
plants.tip: The nest frond collects leaf litter and the plant feeds on it. Do not clean the cup out.
plants.colour: Green antler fronds above a tall brown shield

plants.name: Platycerium wallichii
plants.tip: It drops its fertile fronds in winter and looks dead. Cut watering right back and wait for spring.
plants.colour: Grey-green fronds with a pale shield, deciduous

plants.name: Platycerium stemaria
plants.tip: An African species that resents cold. A chilly windowsill in winter blackens the frond tips first.
plants.colour: Dark green forked fronds, triangular shield

plants.name: Platycerium elephantotis
plants.tip: The undivided fronds scorch in direct sun. Bright shade and warmth, with a dry spell between soakings.
plants.colour: Plain undivided green fronds, no forking

plants.name: Platycerium andinum
plants.tip: The only staghorn from the Americas, and a cloud forest plant: cool nights, moving air, never sodden.
plants.colour: Long narrow grey-green fronds, upright shield

plants.name: Platycerium madagascariense
plants.tip: The honeycombed shield holds water in its ridges. Give it humidity, but keep air moving or those ridges rot.
plants.colour: Bright green fronds over a honeycombed shield

plants.name: Platycerium ellisii
plants.tip: Wants warmth and humidity the year round, and dislikes hard water. Use rainwater if you have it.
plants.colour: Glossy mid-green, shallowly forked fronds

plants.name: Platycerium quadridichotomum
plants.tip: It comes from a seasonally dry forest and needs a real winter rest. Water very sparingly until growth returns.
plants.colour: Grey-green fronds forking repeatedly, four ways

plants.name: Platycerium bifurcatum 'Netherlands'
plants.tip: The commercial staghorn, and the forgiving one. A weekly soak in bright shade is the whole method.
plants.colour: Broad grey-green fronds, tan shield

plants.name: Platycerium bifurcatum 'Mickey's Rainbow'
plants.tip: The crested growth is slower than plain bifurcatum. Feed lightly rather than pushing it.
plants.colour: Green fronds with crested, ruffled tips

plants.name: Platycerium bifurcatum 'Maui'
plants.tip: Broad upright fronds that catch water in the crown. Soak the mount, then tip the water out.
plants.colour: Broad upright grey-green fronds

plants.name: Platycerium hillii 'Panama'
plants.tip: Denser and tidier than the species, and wants the same weekly soak with good air around the mount.
plants.colour: Compact dark green fronds, tight shield

plants.name: Platycerium veitchii 'Lemoinei'
plants.tip: The upright fronds take more direct sun than most staghorns. Full shade makes it floppy and green.
plants.colour: Narrow upright fronds with a heavy silver coat

plants.name: Platycerium veitchii 'Auburn River'
plants.tip: The silver holds only in strong light. In a dim spot new fronds come out green and stay that way.
plants.colour: Dense silver fronds on a compact plant

plants.name: Platycerium veitchii 'Lisa'
plants.tip: Blunt-tipped fronds mark it out. Same dry-tolerant care as the species, in the brightest spot you have.
plants.colour: Silver fronds with wide, blunt tips

plants.name: Platycerium veitchii 'Pumilum'
plants.tip: A half-size veitchii that dries out quicker than it looks. Check the mount rather than the calendar.
plants.colour: Half-size silver fronds, held upright

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Jade Girl'
plants.tip: The heavy silver is trichome, not dust. Water at the base and never try to mist the fronds clean.
plants.colour: Thick silver coat over jade-green fronds

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Smurf'
plants.tip: The narrow blue-green fronds burn easily. Bright shade and humidity, out of any direct afternoon sun.
plants.colour: Narrow blue-green fronds with a silver haze

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Spur'
plants.tip: It forks early and unevenly, which is the whole point of it. Do not tidy the growth back.
plants.colour: Silver-grey fronds forking early into spurs

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Nano'
plants.tip: A dwarf that still wants full willinckii humidity. On a small mount it dries out in a day or two.
plants.colour: Dwarf silver-grey ribbon fronds

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Silky White'
plants.tip: The white coat rubs off with handling and does not grow back on that frond. Move it by the mount.
plants.colour: Even white trichome coat, near-white fronds

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Snow White'
plants.tip: Heavier and less pendulous than other willinckii. Give it a firm mount and room to hang clear.
plants.colour: Broad fronds with a bright white cast

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Celso Tatsuta'
plants.tip: The wide fronds hold water in the crown. Soak from below and let it drain before hanging it back.
plants.colour: Wide silver fronds, heavily furred

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Masayu'
plants.tip: The trichome coat needs light to develop. Too little and the fronds come through plain green.
plants.colour: Wide silver fronds with pronounced shields

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Payton'
plants.tip: A Java-type willinckii with long trailing fronds. Hang it high and let them fall clear of the wall.
plants.colour: Long trailing silver-green ribbons

plants.name: Platycerium willinckii 'Pygmaeum'
plants.tip: Wider fronds on a smaller plant. Treat it as a full willinckii for humidity, not as a beginner's fern.
plants.colour: Wide silver fronds on a small plant

plants.name: Platycerium ridleyi 'Pakarang'
plants.tip: The coral-like fronds snap if knocked. Site it where nothing brushes past, and keep the air moving.
plants.colour: Green shield, fronds branching like coral

plants.name: Platycerium ridleyi 'Dwarf Silver'
plants.tip: Compact shields still rot at the bud if water sits behind them. Soak the mount, never the crown.
plants.colour: Small silver-green shields, narrow fronds

plants.name: Platycerium alcicorne 'Gorgon'
plants.tip: The twisting fronds trap water between them. Water in the morning so they dry before nightfall.
plants.colour: Mid-green fronds, heavily divided and twisting

plants.name: Platycerium 'Charles Alford'
plants.tip: A wandae by ridleyi hybrid, with ridleyi's intolerance of a wet crown. Warmth and airflow decide it.
plants.colour: Green ridged shield with long divided fronds
